verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.124). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The two-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: molar specific heat capacity C = ΔQ/(nΔT), SI unit J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat needed to raise the temperature of one mole of a substance through one degree — a per-MOLE quantity, distinct from the per-unit-mass specific heat capacity S of vsaq6.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: of a substance is the heat needed
to raise the temperature of one
mole of it through one degree.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say it is per mole, not per unit mass.
steps.why: The word molar signals the heat is measured per MOLE of substance, in contrast to the specific heat capacity, which is per unit mass.
common_mistakes: Writing the same definition as specific heat capacity with mass in place of mole — the two are different quantities.
Leaving out one mole and saying only unit quantity.

recall.must_convey: That molar specific heat capacity is the heat needed to raise the temperature of one mole of a substance through one degree.
reject: heat per unit mass per degree

steps.memory_tip: Molar means per mole — swap mass for the mole count n.

steps.label: Formula and unit
lines: Writing n for the number of moles,
steps.margin_note: Second mark. C = ΔQ/(nΔT), SI unit J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
steps.why: Writing n for the number of moles in the denominator is what makes C a per-mole quantity, mirroring the form S = (1/m)(dQ/dT) of the specific heat capacity, which is per unit mass.
common_mistakes: Writing m for mass in place of n for moles — that turns C back into the per-mass specific heat capacity.
Giving the unit as J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, the per-mass unit, instead of J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That C equals delta Q over n delta T, with n the number of moles, SI unit joule per mole per kelvin.
accept: C equals delta Q by n delta T
n is the number of moles
reject: S equals one by m dQ by dT
heard_as: delta Q by n delta T

steps.memory_tip: n for moles in the formula, mol⁻¹ in the unit — both say per mole.

insider_note: C is per MOLE — contrast directly with S, the specific heat capacity, which is per unit MASS. Mixing the two symbols is the commonest slip on this pair.
